results.answer: The 30-day target for NordChemica is to reduce actionable alerts to 500 or fewer per day. Additionally, an immediate reduction of 70% in actionable alerts is promised within 7 days of deploying the suppression tuning bundle. These commitments are part of the remediation plan to address the alert noise issue and satisfy procurement's requirements during renewal negotiations [art_0a135c689c08, art_ffa7143fb822].

The NordChemica remediation plan proposes an EN-DEDUPE sliding-window setting of 5 minutes (300 seconds) with pattern-based grouping by service, host, and event_type. Additionally, the per-host rate limit set for heartbeat-missing-v1 is 1 per minute. These settings are part of the suppression tuning bundle scheduled for delivery on 2026-03-22 to reduce noisy alerting and improve alert signal quality [art_ffa7143fb822].

The contractual financial remedy offered to NordChemica is a conditional 6% credit on their contract for the next year. This credit is tied to specific success metrics: reducing actionable alerts by 70% within 7 days and achieving 500 or fewer actionable alerts per day within 30 days after deployment of the suppression tuning bundle, measured against an agreed analytics baseline. If these targets are not met, the 6% credit will be applied as a financial concession. The credit and its conditions are to be legally approved and documented as part of the renewal negotiation. The baseline report to establish the starting point for these metrics is due by 2026-03-20 end of day, the suppression tuning bundle is scheduled for delivery by 2026-03-22, and a dry-run to validate changes is planned from 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-25 [art_ffa7143fb822, art_0a135c689c08]. 

The exact contractual wording or document reference for the credit clause beyond the negotiation context and planned legal approval is not provided in the evidence.

The temporary Signal Ingest transform (SI-ETL-FILTER) for Aurora University's Ontario campus populates canonical.student_id by concatenating the region_code, a hyphen, and the local.student_number if the event contains local.student_number and not canonical.student_id, while preserving local.student_number in the original field. Additionally, the transform adds a metadata field ingest.transform_version with the value "aurora-v1" to the event. This transform is non-destructive and scoped only to the aurora tenant. The transform version bump is recorded in the Signal Ingest schema registry with backward compatibility. These details come from the temporary ingest mapping and escalation recovery plan dated 2026-03-19, describing the short-term solution for the Ontario campus launch on 2026-02-28 [art_db3975cc8475].

The rollback window for the Aurora Ontario production deploy is 60 minutes. The automatic safeguard that triggers a disable is if more than 2% message drop is observed during the deploy [art_db3975cc8475].

The mapping events failed primarily due to inconsistencies in SCIM mappings and approval chain variants across departments after Northpoint Apparel's HR restructure effective 2026-02-15. Specifically, about 30% of the failed events were caused by the 'role' attribute missing in ServiceNow 'store' catalog webhooks, while for the corporate catalog, the role attribute was present but under a legacy key 'job_code'. These discrepancies led to approximately 9,000 failed mapping events out of 28,000 provisioning-related events, resulting in increased median provisioning latency from about 3.5 hours pre-change to roughly 18 hours post-change [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_fceed52dcb35].

Northstar recommended a fix that involved several coordinated actions:

1. Immediate staging of an ETL normalization filter (SI-ETL-FILTER) in non-production starting 2026-03-19 to map the legacy 'job_code' key to the expected 'role' attribute, provide fallback heuristics, and tag all normalized events. This aimed to harmonize the SCIM mappings and reduce mapping failures [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_fceed52dcb35].

2. Implementation of an Orchestrator playbook to automatically retry provisioning for the store catalog and perform dry-run re-triggers for the corporate catalog. This playbook would include audit logs (OR-AUDIT-LOGS) and safe rollback capabilities (OR-SAFE-ROLLBACK) to ensure safe remediation without disrupting operations [art_ab3362f35c1b].

3. Building a Signal Insights dashboard to monitor provisioning latency, failed mapping counters, collector buffer health, and re-trigger audit events, with the first snapshot scheduled for 2026-03-26. This would provide operational visibility and support SLA reporting for the board by 2026-04-15 [art_ab3362f35c1b].

4. Modifying the retention policy for provisioning logs to 365 days to support auditability, with an expected 12% increase in storage cost [art_ab3362f35c1b].

The remediation plan was approved on 2026-03-18, with coordination led by Carlos Mendes and technical leads Daniel Kim (Ingest) and Jin Park (Orchestrator). The fix aimed to reduce the median provisioning latency back toward pre-change levels (~3.5 hours) [art_ab3362f35c1b].

Additional support tickets confirmed the failure modes, including malformed SCIM attributes and lack of retry logic in orchestration playbooks, which Northstar addressed by recommending per-department SCIM filters and retry/backoff mechanisms in Orchestrator playbooks with audit trails [art_9d3bef4ff8f4].

In summary, the mapping failures were caused by inconsistent SCIM attribute keys and webhook variants across departments, and Northstar's fix was to normalize these mappings via an ETL filter, implement automated retry orchestration with audit and rollback, and enhance monitoring and retention for operational and audit purposes [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_fceed52dcb35, art_9d3bef4ff8f4].

If the validation checks fail for Verdant Bay's live patch, the system will automatically roll back to the pre-patch ruleset as per the established playbook. The rollback procedure involves running the command `orchestrator rollback --target ruleset=<prior_sha>`, which rehydrates the prior rules and replays the cache invalidation hook to restore the previous state. After rollback, the team must notify Verdant Bay, open an incident for manual remediation, and revert any partial replays that may have occurred. This rollback is integrated into the live patch deployment scheduled for 2026-03-24 02:00-04:00 local time, ensuring safety and minimal disruption by including pre-patch snapshots and worker pool draining before deployment. The validation jobs that trigger this rollback include running 50 synthetic approval flows and sampling 50 in-flight approvals marked by the customer; any failure in these checks leads to the automatic rollback execution [art_fff67d92fe41]. 

Details such as step-by-step commands beyond the single CLI command, specific failure thresholds, rollback timing guarantees, or post-rollback verification procedures beyond notification and incident opening are not provided in the evidence.
